pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — MOCK EXAM #9
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is polite when you collect a song from an elder? (1 mark)
   A. Greet them and thank them at the end
   B. Refuse to listen
   C. Take the song without asking
   D. Interrupt while they sing

2. What does fluent reading mean? (1 mark)
   A. Reading in a whisper
   B. Skipping words
   C. Reading smoothly without stopping at every word
   D. Reading very slowly word by word

3. What is a good first step when reading for information? (1 mark)
   A. Guess the ending
   B. Copy the title
   C. Ask what you want to find out
   D. Close the book

4. Tall letters such as b and d usually reach (1 mark)
   A. the edge of the desk
   B. below the base line
   C. the bottom of the page
   D. the top line

5. Which is a mistake in reading aloud? (1 mark)
   A. Practising first
   B. Pausing at full stops
   C. Reading too fast so nobody can follow
   D. Looking up at the audience

6. How do you show a question when reading aloud? (1 mark)
   A. Raise your voice at the end
   B. Read it faster
   C. Stop reading
   D. Whisper

7. How are words arranged in a dictionary? (1 mark)
   A. By the number of letters
   B. By colour
   C. By size of the word
   D. In alphabetical order

8. Which word shows the first step? (1 mark)
   A. First
   B. Lastly
   C. In the end
   D. Finally

9. Which word shows the last step in a sequence? (1 mark)
   A. First
   B. Begin
   C. Next
   D. Finally

10. What is a simile? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of song
   B. A saying with no comparison
   C. A long story
   D. A comparison using like or as

11. Which words signal a simile? (1 mark)
   A. but and or
   B. is and are
   C. to and from
   D. like and as

12. What is an imaginative composition? (1 mark)
   A. A story made from the imagination
   B. A list of prices
   C. A weather forecast
   D. A news report

13. What should you do if a stranger promises cheap goods and asks for money first? (1 mark)
   A. Be careful and ask an adult
   B. Trust them
   C. Send money at once
   D. Give your address

14. What is profit? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of shop
   B. A bill
   C. Money spent
   D. Money left after paying the cost

15. In The seller counts the money, what is the predicate? (1 mark)
   A. The seller
   B. counts the money
   C. The
   D. money only

16. What is a receipt? (1 mark)
   A. A paper that shows you paid
   B. A type of fruit
   C. A shop
   D. A kind of coin

17. Which of these is a preposition? (1 mark)
   A. behind
   B. quickly
   C. banana
   D. jump

18. Which of these is a character? (1 mark)
   A. A girl called Neema
   B. Under the tree
   C. A cloudy afternoon
   D. The last page

19. What are the events of a story? (1 mark)
   A. The author
   B. The title
   C. The margin
   D. What happens step by step

20. What is a stage direction? (1 mark)
   A. A price
   B. The ending
   C. The title
   D. An instruction to the actor placed in brackets

21. What is an adjective? (1 mark)
   A. A joining word
   B. A word that names a person
   C. A word that describes a noun
   D. A word that shows action

22. Which word in an advert may be used to persuade? (1 mark)
   A. table
   B. door
   C. best
   D. paper

23. What is a digital form? (1 mark)
   A. A form made of clay
   B. A form on a tree
   C. A form filled in on a device
   D. A paper airplane

24. Which is a part of a form? (1 mark)
   A. Poem
   B. Riddle
   C. Title
   D. Ending song

25. Which word in The teacher counted the votes is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. counted
   B. the
   C. teacher
   D. votes

26. Which is a rude phrase? (1 mark)
   A. Shut up
   B. Excuse me
   C. Please continue
   D. Pardon me

27. What does a class monitor do? (1 mark)
   A. Runs the school
   B. Helps lead the class
   C. Cooks
   D. Drives

28. What are non-verbal cues in a performance? (1 mark)
   A. Written words
   B. Loud shouting
   C. Gestures and facial expressions
   D. Music only

29. What is the treasure hunt game used for? (1 mark)
   A. Sleeping
   B. Learning to sing
   C. Practising following instructions
   D. Drawing maps only

30. Which word helps to show the order of steps? (1 mark)
   A. Finally
   B. Yesterday
   C. Green
   D. Table

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Explain how the language train game is played. (4 marks)

32. Explain when you would skim and when you would scan. Give one example of each. (5 marks)

33. Give three rules for writing clear instructions. (3 marks)

34. Give three qualities of a good leader mentioned in the model poem lead with honesty. (3 marks)

35. Name three questions to ask yourself before telling a personal experience. (3 marks)

36. Explain the difference in punctuation between Wow! and Oops, it is torn. (3 marks)

37. Explain how to take part in a class handwriting gallery walk. (4 marks)

38. Explain what turn taking means. (2 marks)

39. Explain two differences between an advert and a news item. (4 marks)

40. Explain what intonation is and give one English example of a rising voice. (2 marks)

41. Write one simile and one metaphor about a teacher. (3 marks)

42. Name three ways to practise letter shapes before writing them. (3 marks)

43. Give three questions to ask when reading an advert. (3 marks)

44. Read: Millet porridge is a warm drink made by mixing millet flour with water and boiling it. What is it made from and how is it cooked? (3 marks)

45. Give three tips for telling a story well. (3 marks)

46. Mama Neema buys a box of bananas for 200 shillings and sells it for 260 shillings. Find her profit. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — MOCK EXAM #9 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — Greet them and thank them at the end
   Good manners include greeting, listening and thanking.

2. C — Reading smoothly without stopping at every word
   Fluent readers read smoothly.

3. C — Ask what you want to find out
   A question in mind helps you look for the right facts.

4. D — the top line
   Tall letters go up to the top line.

5. C — Reading too fast so nobody can follow
   Speed that is too fast loses meaning.

6. A — Raise your voice at the end
   Questions often rise at the end.

7. D — In alphabetical order
   Dictionaries use alphabetical order.

8. A — First
   First begins the sequence.

9. D — Finally
   Finally is used for the last step.

10. D — A comparison using like or as
   A simile compares two things using like or as.

11. D — like and as
   Similes use like or as.

12. A — A story made from the imagination
   Imaginative compositions are made-up stories.

13. A — Be careful and ask an adult
   Such offers may be tricks.

14. D — Money left after paying the cost
   Profit is gain after costs.

15. B — counts the money
   The predicate tells what the subject does.

16. A — A paper that shows you paid
   A receipt is proof of payment.

17. A — behind
   Behind shows position.

18. A — A girl called Neema
   Characters are people or animals.

19. D — What happens step by step
   Events are the actions in order.

20. D — An instruction to the actor placed in brackets
   Stage directions tell how to speak or move.

21. C — A word that describes a noun
   Adjectives describe nouns.

22. C — best
   Words such as best persuade people to buy.

23. C — A form filled in on a device
   Digital forms are filled on phones or computers.

24. C — Title
   A form has a title.

25. A — counted
   Counted shows the action.

26. A — Shut up
   Shut up is disrespectful.

27. B — Helps lead the class
   A monitor helps the teacher lead.

28. C — Gestures and facial expressions
   Non-verbal cues are actions without words.

29. C — Practising following instructions
   Each note gives the next instruction.

30. A — Finally
   Finally shows the last step.

SECTION B
----
31. (4 marks)
   Answer: A pupil starts with a sentence. Each next pupil continues the story with a sentence beginning with when until the story ends.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four points.

32. (5 marks)
   Answer: Skim when you want the main idea, for example looking through an article. Scan when you want one fact, for example looking for a name on a list.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for the two situations and two marks for examples and one mark for correct meaning.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: Put steps in order, begin each step with a verb, use short sentences, one action per step, add warnings.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: Fair, true, listens, shares the work, kind, strong (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: Who was there, what happened, where, when, why, how did I feel.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each question.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: An exclamation mark shows strong feeling, and a comma after a mild interjection shows a softer feeling.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each punctuation mark and one for the difference.

37. (4 marks)
   Answer: Write your best sentence on a strip. Display it on the wall. Walk quietly, look at each strip, and leave a kind and helpful comment.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four points.

38. (2 marks)
   Answer: It means speaking one person at a time and waiting for others to finish before speaking.
   Working / marking points: One mark for one at a time and one for waiting.

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: An advert aims to persuade people to buy, while news informs about events. An advert gives a price and where to buy, while news gives who, what, where and when.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for each difference.

40. (2 marks)
   Answer: Intonation is the rise and fall of the voice as we speak. A question such as Are you coming? rises at the end.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and one mark for a correct example.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Simile: The teacher is as patient as a rock. Metaphor: The teacher is a walking dictionary.
   Working / marking points: One mark for a simile, one for a metaphor, one for clearly showing the difference.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Trace in the air, trace on a card, model with clay or string, paint them.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each way.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: What is being sold, who is it for, what is the price, where can I get it, is it as good as it says.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: It is made from millet flour and water and it is cooked by boiling.
   Working / marking points: One mark for millet flour, one for water, one for boiling.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Start with a clear opening, tell events in order, speak clearly, look at the audience, end with what you learned.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each tip.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: 260 minus 200 equals 60 shillings.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the working and one mark for the answer with units.
